correctness.rationale: Eliminating y gives x_{−1}=0 and x_{n+1}=τ_±x_n−δx_{n−1}+μ with branch selected by x_n. With q=μ/α the formal incoming deficit is q−x_n=Aλ^n+Bρ^n for distinct roots, with A=(λ(h+q)−δq)/(λ−ρ)>0 and limit hλ/(λ−ρ). At δ=t² the matrix is defective (off-diagonal entry 1), and the two initial values give q−x_n=[h+q+n(h+(1−t)q)]t^n. In either case the formal deficit stays positive, tends to zero, and all fixed indices remain negative in x as q→0. Thus the actual switch agrees with the first crossing N of this formal deficit below q. Adjacent deficit ratios at N are bounded away from zero and converge to the appropriate stable root, even as q varies. They bracket the threshold, making both x_N and x_{N−1} O(q). At the Jordan edge, the bracket in the deficit divided by hN equals 1+(1−t)q/h+(1+q/h)/N, tending to 1. Consequently aN−log N=L+O(1), a=|log t|, which first implies N∼L/a and then N=(L+log L)/a+O(1). The simple-root case instead has N=L/|log λ|+O(1). On the outgoing side, x_{n+1}−x_n=αx_n+δ(x_n−x_{n−1})+μ is positive inductively, including exact x_N=0. With u=x+q, the unstable coefficient is (γu_0−δu_{−1})/(γ−ζ), bounded above and below by positive multiples of q since u_0≥q and u_{−1}<q; the stable coefficient is O(q). The first outgoing crossing therefore takes L/log γ+O(1) steps. This verifies actual discrete passage, not an inadmissible branch extension.
